## Series Overview

This five-part series is my own coding-first walkthrough of the agentic-AI design
patterns taught in DeepLearning.AI's *Agentic AI* short course (Andrew Ng). All the
underlying ideas — tool use, planning, reflection, evaluation/error analysis, and
multi-agent systems — come from that course. What's different here: every example is
rebuilt from scratch around **image segmentation**, and specifically the kind of
segmentation I do daily on semiconductor inspection images (X-ray void detection, AOI,
USM). None of the code copies the course's lab notebooks line-for-line — I used them as
a starting point, found gaps, and rebuilt the exercises around segmentation images
instead of the course's original (non-imaging) examples.

Each post maps one course concept onto one stage of a segmentation pipeline, and the
series is deliberately not a straight linear pipeline: Part 5 makes the case for putting
the error-analysis agent at the *center* of the design, routing fixes back to whichever
component needs them, instead of treating error analysis as a dead-end report at the
end of the line.

### Posts in this series

1. [Building an Image-Preprocessing Agent](01-preprocessing-agent.qmd) — tool use /
   function calling, letting an LLM choose and sequence deterministic preprocessing
   steps (percentile normalization, tiling, saturation QC) instead of hard-coding them.
2. [Building a Training-Planner Agent](02-training-agent.qmd) — the planning pattern:
   JSON plans you can review before spending GPU-hours, and code-as-plan for more
   open-ended training requests.
3. [Building a Postprocessing-Reflection Agent](03-postprocessing-agent.qmd) — the
   cheapest, highest-leverage pattern in the course: generate → critique against
   objective domain rules (containment violations, blob noise) → regenerate.
4. [Building a Segmentation Error-Analysis Agent](04-error-analysis-agent.qmd) — the
   centerpiece of the series. Reading failure traces, tallying root cause by pipeline
   component, and prioritizing fixes by frequency × fixability instead of by whichever
   failure looks most dramatic.
5. [A Multi-Agent Segmentation Pipeline](05-multiagent-system.qmd) — wiring all four
   agents together with the error-analysis agent as manager, so a dominant failure mode
   routes straight back to the agent responsible for fixing it.

## Tools used throughout

- Local inference via vLLM — `Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B` for text/code agents,
  `Qwen3-VL-32B-FP8` for vision-language judging, run on an NVIDIA DGX Spark
  (Grace-Blackwell GB10, 128GB unified memory)
- MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers so the same tools work from a hand-written
  Python loop or from Copilot/Claude Code agent mode
- Real semiconductor-imaging domain rules throughout: p2/p98 percentile X-ray
  normalization, chip-containment checks, IoU/Dice evals

:::{.callout-note}
This series pairs well with the [Local-AI Defect Inspection Series](../local-ai-defect-inspection/index.qmd),
which covers fine-tuning and evaluating small local VLMs on the same class of imagery.
:::
